audience_note: Describes forced mass deportation with deaths in transit, killings of people unable to travel, and destroyed villages. Death tolls are contested, and some sources call the event genocide.
title: Deportation of the Chechens and Ingush (Operation Lentil)
summary: Beginning on 23 February 1944, Soviet NKVD and army units rounded up roughly half a million Chechens and Ingush in the North Caucasus and deported them in freight trains, mainly to Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. The Chechen-Ingush republic was abolished. Many thousands died in transit and in exile; the stated pretext was alleged collaboration with Germany.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the end of transports as 9 or 13 March 1944; one gives completion for the Ingush by 28 February.

as_recorded.value: began on February 23, 1944 at 02:00 local time and ended on March 9 of the same year

where.modern_name: Chechnya and Ingushetia, Russia (pin at Grozny)
where.historical_name: Chechen-Ingush Autonomous Soviet Socialist Republic, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union (capital Grozny)

importance.justification: One of the largest Soviet wartime ethnic deportations; it shaped Chechen and Ingush memory and later conflicts in the Caucasus.

related.because: One opened source states Stalin approved the operation in October 1943, with Beria directing it.
